propositions: A configured provider is silently discarded when a model id contains a colon (e.g., versioned Bedrock ids like 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' are returned unqualified instead of prefixed with the configured provider)
The _resolve_target function incorrectly decides qualification status by testing for colon presence, confusing version suffixes with provider separators
An explicitly configured provider must be checked before scanning the model string, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule the configuration
A conflict between an explicitly configured provider and an already-qualified model string should raise an error rather than silently pick a winner
The same qualification decision was implemented separately in two places (_resolve_target and infer_provider), causing them to drift and fail identically
Unversioned Bedrock aliases work by accident, hiding the bug in versioned canonical ids which are the majority form AWS publishes
